definitions.explanation: The degree to which a tool, device, or service is easy to use. A standard criterion in product reviews and design discussions, alongside price and performance.

examples.japanese: このアプリは{使|つか}いやすさが{評価|ひょうか}されている。
examples.english: This app is praised for its ease of use.

examples.japanese: {値段|ねだん}よりも{使|つか}いやすさを{重視|じゅうし}して{選|えら}んだ。
examples.english: I chose it valuing usability over price.

examples.japanese: {機能|きのう}を{増|ふ}やしすぎると、かえって{使|つか}いやすさが{損|そこ}なわれる。
examples.english: Adding too many features actually harms usability.

examples.japanese: {高齢者|こうれいしゃ}にとっての{使|つか}いやすさを{考|かんが}えて、{文字|もじ}を{大|おお}きくする{設計|せっけい}に{変更|へんこう}した。
examples.english: Considering usability for older people, we changed the design to use larger text.

notes:
The noun form of {使|つか}いやすい (easy to use), made with the 〜さ suffix that turns adjectives into nouns of degree.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {使|つか}いやすさを{重視|じゅうし}する: to place importance on usability
- {使|つか}いやすさが{向上|こうじょう}する: usability improves
- {使|つか}いやすさで{選|えら}ぶ: to choose based on ease of use

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {使|つか}い{勝手|がって}: usability in practice — more colloquial, focused on how a thing feels in daily use
- ユーザビリティ: usability — the loanword, used in design and IT contexts
- {使|つか}いにくさ: awkwardness to use — the direct opposite
